paper.title: Pareto-optimal Non-uniform Language Generation
paper.summary: Constructs canonical Pareto-optimal language-wise generation times, realizes arbitrarily large finite prefixes and exact vectors under finite sublevels, and extends the framework to noisy and representative non-uniform generation.

formalization_scope.summary: Theorems 1, 4, and 5 are formalized at a distinct-history semantic boundary. A totalized repair of noisy Procedure 2 supplies concrete Theorems 6 and 8. Representative Theorem 7 is unformalized, and Theorem 9 currently has only its conditional finite-sublevel scheduler endgame.
specializations: The indexed collection is represented explicitly as F : Nat -> Set alpha, preserving the source ordering and possible duplicate languages.
Standard and noisy generation guarantees use injective finite histories whose cardinality is the number of distinct observations; no repeated-history adapter is exposed.
The development is classical and semantic and makes no extracted-executability or running-time claim.
gaps: The representative partition, distributional output semantics, group-scarcity condition, Procedure 3, Claim C.2, and concrete Theorems 7 and 9 remain open.
The source's repeated-observation interface is not yet connected to the injective distinct-history theorem surface.
No P13 claim currently has a human statement-correspondence audit.

audit_refs.scope: Direct AI-assisted comparison of all seven headline theorem groups against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v1 PDF, including the Procedure 2 repair and the unformalized representative branch; no human certification is claimed.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for every claim-linked P13 declaration.

claim_inventory.scope_description: The seven headline theorem groups: overview Theorem 1 and detailed Theorems 4--9.
exclusions: Definitions, Claims 3.1--3.2 and B.1--B.3, Propositions 3.3--3.4, Procedures 1--3, proof equations, and proof-only invariants are documented in the PaperMap rather than separate claim cards.
Prior-work statements, examples, remarks, and open questions are outside this headline-result inventory.
claim_inventory.notes: The source inventory is complete even though Lean coverage is not: complete coverage is recorded for the standard headline results and corrected noisy results, while the representative branch remains explicitly partial or unformalized.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: Stable Overview endpoints for every covered headline result plus the conditional Theorem-9 scheduler core.
exclusions: Theorem 7 has no Lean endpoint because its representative distributional construction is not formalized.
Canonical proof declarations, source diagnostics, proposition endpoints, constructors, and internal invariants are documented in the PaperMap but are not duplicate headline claim links.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: The linked declarations are all exposed through GenLimit.ParetoGeneration.Results.

claims.title: Almost Pareto-optimal non-uniform language generation
claims.statement_summary: For every finite prefix of an indexed language collection, one non-uniform generator realizes generation times matching the canonical Procedure-1 vector on that prefix, and no realizable vector can improve a prefix coordinate without worsening another prefix coordinate.

source_assessment.notes: Lean states the theorem at the injective distinct-history semantic boundary and uses the corrected max-score form of Claim 3.2.

formalization.notes: The Overview wrapper delegates to the concrete Procedure-1 construction and prefix Pareto proof.

lean_links.notes: The requested source prefix is represented by a natural-number stage.

relations.notes: Both results use the same Procedure-1 complexity and greedy target-selection invariant.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the Theorem 1 Results wrapper; source correspondence remains AI-assisted.

claims.title: Non-uniform generation times for an arbitrary scheduler
claims.statement_summary: Every monotone unbounded scheduler drives a generator whose language-wise time is the maximum of scheduler entry time and canonical non-uniform complexity plus one.

source_assessment.notes: The displayed time vector is preserved exactly; Lean uses the injective distinct-history interface and corrected Claim 3.2 invariant.

formalization.notes: The source generalized inverse g is the schedulerEntryTime definition.

lean_links.notes: The wrapper exposes both the achieved vector and its positivity.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the Theorem 4 arbitrary-scheduler Results wrapper; source correspondence remains AI-assisted.

claims.title: Finite sublevels suffice for exact Pareto optimality
claims.statement_summary: If every bounded sublevel of the canonical Procedure-1 complexity contains finitely many indices, one scheduler-driven generator realizes the complete canonical Pareto-optimal time vector.

source_assessment.notes: Lean states the source finiteness condition as FiniteSublevels and inherits the distinct-history boundary of Theorem 4.

formalization.notes: The generic finite-sublevel scheduler is instantiated with canonical Procedure-1 complexity.

lean_links.notes: The theorem packages realization, positivity, and Pareto optimality.

relations.notes: The finite-sublevel scheduler collapses Theorem 4's maximum to canonical complexity plus one.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the Theorem 5 exact-Pareto Results wrapper; source correspondence remains AI-assisted.

claims.title: Noisy non-uniform generation times
claims.statement_summary: A scheduler-driven noisy generator realizes the maximum of diagonal scheduler-entry time and the canonical noisy non-uniform complexity plus one.

source_assessment.notes: The first Step-A optimization in printed Procedure 2 can have no feasible witness. Lean totalizes that branch with an empty witness and zero score while retaining the theorem's displayed time vector.

formalization.notes: The corrected totalized construction discharges the full deterministic semantic theorem.

lean_links.notes: The wrapper makes the totalization part of the named result rather than an unstated premise.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the corrected Theorem 6 Results wrapper; it does not independently validate the source Procedure 2 pseudocode.

claims.title: Representative non-uniform generation times
claims.statement_summary: For a finite partition of the universe, the representative-generation algorithm realizes the maximum of scheduler-entry time and canonical representative complexity plus one while satisfying alpha-representation.

source_assessment.notes: The source theorem has not yet been translated into the repository's representative-generation interfaces.

formalization.notes: The finite-partition distributional semantics, group scarcity, Procedure 3, and concrete scheduler theorem remain open.

claims.title: Finite noisy sublevels suffice for exact Pareto optimality
claims.statement_summary: If every bounded sublevel of the canonical noisy complexity contains finitely many diagonal coordinates, a noisy generator realizes a Pareto-optimal canonical noisy time vector.

source_assessment.notes: The endgame is valid after totalizing Procedure 2's no-candidate initialization.

formalization.notes: The corrected concrete noisy certificate instantiates the common exact-Pareto scheduler theorem.

lean_links.notes: The source finite-sublevel condition is represented directly by FiniteSublevels.

relations.notes: Theorem 6 supplies the scheduler-realizability component of the concrete noisy certificate.

claims.title: Finite representative sublevels suffice for exact Pareto optimality
claims.statement_summary: If every bounded sublevel of the canonical representative complexity is finite, the representative construction admits a Pareto-optimal canonical generation-time vector.

source_assessment.notes: The common scheduling implication is formalized, but the representative construction and Claim C.2 needed to instantiate it are not.

formalization.notes: The finite-sublevel scheduler endgame is complete, but no concrete representative certificate instantiates it.
